text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- More then 67,000 voters in at least 18 municipalities will not be able to vote in September local elections because partners in the Moslem-Croat federation failed to agree on the structure of municipalities which are divided by the inter-entity boundary line (IEBL), Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) says.

- Robert Frowick, head of the OSCE mission, decides local elections in disputed town of Brcko will be held in September with the polling district established in the pre-war Brcko municipality which is now under Serb control. All those who lived in the town before the war have the right to vote.

- More then 50,000 Bosnians in the northwest Una-Sana county in federation territory requested a Croatian passport and many of them have already got it, says Bernardo Jurlina, Croatian consul in Bosnia.

- As for meeting conditions for the international donors' conference on reconstruction, the Council of Ministers has done everything in its power and now the issue is out of its hands, says Haris Silajdzic, Moslem co-prime minister.

- Office of the High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt, suggests that a new Bosnian passport should include the country's emblem, bear the name Bosnia and Herzegovina and specify which of the two entities the citizen lives. But the proposal needs to be approved by the collective presidency, diplomats say.

- NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Doboj says it knows nothing about plans for a federation army offensive against Serb republic in August, alleged by Bosnian Serb army commander Pero Colic. But SFOR is closely watching movements of all the armies in Bosnia and is ready to react if needed.

- Leaders of Bosnian branch of Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), after a recent meeting with Croatian President and HDZ leader Franjo Tudjman in Zagreb, begin to speak about Bosnia as an integral country of strategic interest to all Croats. If their comments signal a shift in policy, it would be good news for Bosnia, commentary says.
- Britain, Canada and Japan will donate $44.8 milion for reconstruction of the country's electrical production network, federation minister of energy, Izudin Kapetanovic, says.

- Leader of opposition Union of Bosnian Social Democrats, Sejfudin Tokic, asks for resignation of the Moslem-Croat federation minister of interior, Mehmed Zilic, after police detained a deputy in the federation parliament, Ibrahim Djedovic, as an alleged war crimes suspect. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387 71 663 864
